newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz to ask president's approval Monday.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz to ask president's approval Monday.

text.p: Turkish prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz plans to ask President Suleyman Demirel on Monday to approve his proposed anti-Islamist coalition government, newspapers said.
"The government is ready. I will announce the cabinet list tomorrow," the Hurriyet daily quoted Yilmaz as saying on Sunday. Other papers carried similar stories.

The Anatolian news agency said on Sunday that Yilmaz and his two coalition partners were close to agreement on a protocol outlining the new government's policies and the distribution of cabinet seats.
Yilmaz was asked by the president to prepare a new government after Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, the first Islamist to lead modern Turkey, resigned earlier this month.
Under Turkish law, the president must approve a new government before it goes to a parliamentary confidence vote within 10 days.
Three more members of parliament resigned at the weekend from a pro-Islamist alliance, further boosting Yilmaz's hopes of winning the confidence vote.
